reviews.text:
Lots of current issues, all fixable. The bad: Generally over engineered, unintuitive. Lacks video examples of women performing exercises. Buggy: have lost multiple workout sessions due to workouts getting stuck and unable to complete. Way too many clicks to just see what I did on an exercise last session. Doesn’t tell me the name of the workout in the history logs. Can’t see actual set logs from dashboard. Appears to use some weird rolling window algo to calculate 1rm instead of discrete logged sets so that even when I lift less with the same weight my 1rm goes up for that session. Doesn’t allow you to change your logged set’s weight or reps without resetting rest timer. Exercise naming conventions are precise but hard to recognize on dash board when cutoff: half my exercises just say “Plate-Loaded…” or “Overhand Grip Pin Loaded…” and never get to the only thing I want to see there which is “Shoulder Press” or “Machine Row”. Can’t search for exercises to add to dashboard, must scroll through everything. Impossible to add two of the same exact workout to a single cycle without duplicating it, resulting in duplicating work when adding/removing exercises from that workout. The time estimates for a workout are wildly inaccurate, completely underselling how long a given workout will take. To make a point I plugged in Jeff’s own “45 minute leg routine” and the app guessed it would take 14 minutes. 

The good: sleek ui. Easily swap exercises during a session. Easy to add/remove sets or exercises during a session. Extremely wide and precise available exercise selection. Easily see number of sets per muscle per week

Insane value. MAKE sure to coach yourself too!. I had been using MacroFactor, the nutrition app, on and off for about a year and was excitedly waiting for the workouts app to come out to have cohesion with the data and user flow. 

The app is a dream and such a natural extension of the regular MacroFactor app, which has been receiving a lot of support and updates over the time I've been using it as well. There are waay more things to like and love than dislike about both of these apps. 

One thing to keep in mind while doing the workouts is to *stay present in your body* and be aware of when you're starting to feel:
1. Any pain
2. Lower range of motion
3. Tingling or other sensations in your muscles

It can be easy to push yourself with this app since it wants to help you get stronger and stronger, and it often puts higher and higher weight loads on you in ways that can seem pretty fast for me at times. 

YOU are your ground truth, not stats and plans in an app.

It’s alright, definitely better out there though.. After using MacroFactor for a year or so, I was excited to learn that Jeff Nippard came out with a new app similar to it but for working out. However, after using it for a few weeks, it is fairly lack luster compared to other training apps out there such as “the train app.” So here’s the pros and cons.

The pros:

The app is definitely nice. It used the same formula as the macro factor app to make workouts for you. This is extremely nice especially when you want to gain strength. Specifically, I think the best feature of this app is its ability to help you find the correct weight for each set. So far in my workouts, the app is mostly spot on. If I’m doing leg curls and the app recommends 11 reps at x weight… 11 reps is nearly perfect every-time. Along with this the feature that is has for each rep range, such as failure or 2 reps in reserve, is very convenient and really helps you stay on track each workout. The next biggest pro is that the app has, I think, EVERY possible exercise there is at any gym. 

The cons: 

While the pros of this app are definitely big time pros the cons make it hard to really say the app is worth it compared to other training apps. For one, the alert for when it’s time for your set is not great. Yes it will give you a little bell but other apps I’ve used will give you multiple alerts. For example, if I’m doing a set and the rest time is 1:30 at 30 seconds I’ll get an alert in my AirPods saying “30 seconds” repeat at 15 seconds and then a count down at 5 and it automatically turns up the music. The workouts app does not do this and only gives a small bell as an indicator to a set. Next, other apps will actually connect to your Apple Watch. A big plus to this is that they also track the reps you do (if it’s an upper body exercise or a squat like exercise of course). Sadly the workouts app does not, in my opinion this really helps in the gym as you do ever have to count reps and can just focus on the exercise and mind muscle connection itself. The last con I have is actually just some of the exercises that are suggested themselves. While I’m sure they must be the greatest exercises scientifically for muscle growth. Some of these exercises suggested do feel like a waste of time. Nordic hamstring curls are great for a high school football team that may not have a big enough weight room for everyone to get reps in. However, Nordic hamstring curls are not good if you’re at a gym and have multiple machines to hit hamstrings and glutes. 

With all this said, I would recommend this app to anyone who has used MacroFactor in the past or if you’re new to the gym. However if you’re experienced in the gym, there are other apps that are just better.

Amazing app by awesome people. I’ve been using the nutrition app for about 6 months now, and it has helped me in so many ways. So of course, when the same team announced a workout app, I was stoked.
I thought I was relatively good in my workouts, and with a custom made workout routine that I was very comfortable with, I was hesitant to try out the app’s workout plan. However, I figured I could give it a try for a week at least, and if I didn’t like it I’d just go back to my old routine.
Well, the week is up, and I am absolutely sticking with the app’s plan. Somehow my body is tired in ways that it has never been tired before, but I don’t feel worn out. Does that even make sense? I love the adjustability and the ease of use. All I did was pick a few focus areas, tell it how long I wanted to work out, how many days, and if I preferred full body or split workouts. Boom, workout plan done. It has targeted my selected groups well, while still making sure that the rest of my body is getting trained. I’m doing exercises I’ve never even seen before, but the video tutorials and written explanations make them easy to accomplish. Granted, there are a few minor bugs since the app is still new, but the team behind this app is beyond responsive. If you do download the app, I highly suggest following their Reddit page as well. Any time I’ve had a question I can look it up there, and someone has already asked and gotten an answer. 
Very excited to see the results I get from this workout app, I’m already pushing myself much harder than ever before!

reviews.text:
Initial thoughts. Developers/SBS idea people - 

I think this is an extremely detailed app with a lot of great features and information (s/o Jeff for recording all of the videos). Currently giving this 3 stars but will edit this review as time passes. Obviously take this with a grain of salt as this is one man’s opinion and there are my first impressions as I am still getting comfortable with the app. 

Priority 1 improvements:

1a - Iphone lock screen / “island” compatibility. Having the ability to see what movement you are on without having to toggle the “always on function” seems like a no brainer. I imagine this is coming in future updates. 

1b - The UI in workouts feels a little clunky. I think having the videos up top is the main cause. This is a great feature generally but it would be nice to be able to toggle to a “condensed mode” similar to your ability to “optimize for detail or optimize for speed” / remove untracked hours in the diet app. The other general thing contributing to the “clunky feeling” is that workout edits and swiping to the next workout use the same gesture. For example if I’m swiping through the workouts there is a greater than 0 chance I swipe on a set and the red edit button pops up. All that to say if you implement a “condensed mode” having it scroll vertically might be a good move. 

Priority 2 improvements:
- L/R should be a feature you can put in to the workout plan not just when you start a workout. If I’m doing a single arm lat pull down I will always want a L/R split.
- There are WAY too many exercises not to have search functions for all of the places that you have to scroll. Dashboard customization become difficult when I have to scroll through all the exercises 
- On the swap exercise in workout, it would be cool to have the video function / info function still work. Nothing worse than swapping an exercise and realizing it was the wrong one because the name is similar to another or I was incorrect in choosing.

Finally, an algorithm that understands hypertrophy (Bye Strong!). I’ve been a die-hard user of the MacroFactor nutrition app for years, so when they announced a workout companion, my expectations were sky-high. MacroFactor Workouts exceeds them.

Most workout apps are just digital notebooks you have to guess when to add weight or add sets. This app is different. It brings the same "smart coaching" philosophy to the gym.

True Auto-Regulation: The "Smart Progression" feature is a game changer. It adjusts my targets daily based on my actual performance and RIR (Reps In Reserve). It pushes me when I’m recovering well and pulls back when I’m not. No more guessing if I should add 5lbs or hold steady.

Jeff Nippard’s Library: The exercise library isn't just generic animations, having technique videos from Jeff Nippard built-in is incredible value.

Seamless Integration: Syncing body metrics and recovery data with the nutrition app makes this the most complete fitness ecosystem on the iPhone.

If you are serious about muscle growth and want a program that adapts to you rather than a static PDF, download this now. The bundle pricing with the nutrition app makes it a no-brainer.
